items.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
items.body: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is a key prodromal marker of Parkinson's disease (PD). Video-polysomnography (vPSG) remains the diagnostic gold standard, but manual sleep staging is particularly time-consuming and challenging in neurodegenerative disease. We adapted U-Sleep, a deep neural network, for automated sleep staging in PD and iRBD. A pretrained model (PUB, 19,236 PSGs), was finetuned on multicenter datasets (PACE, CBC: 112 PD, 138 iRBD, 89 controls) and evaluated on a clinical hold-out (DCSM: 81 PD, 36 iRBD, 87 controls). Predictors of staging agreement were analyzed, and low-agreement recordings were blindly rescored. Confidence-based thresholds were applied to enhance REM detection. The pretrained model achieved κ = 0.66 in PACE/CBC, improving to κ = 0.74 after finetuning (p < 0.001). In the hold-out, mean κ increased from 0.60 to 0.64 (p < 0.001). Site-specific finetuning provided minimal benefit. Confidence was a significant predictor of Cohen's κ (p < 0.001). Recordings with low model agreement also showed low human interrater agreement. Applying a confidence threshold increased REM precision from 85 to 95.6%, preserving sufficient REM sleep in 96% of subjects. This publicly available model achieves human-level agreement enabling scalable, standardized PSG analysis with model-derived confidence as a tool for further refinements.
items.why: A deep neural network (U-Sleep) pretrained on 19,236 polysomnograms (PSGs) was finetuned on multicenter Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) cohorts and evaluated on an independent clinical hold-out, improving staging agreement (Cohen's kappa) from 0.60 to 0.64, with a confidence threshold raising REM sleep detection precision from 85% to 95.6%. This is a rare example of a publicly available, externally validated automated sleep staging tool tested specifically in neurodegenerative disease populations where manual scoring is hardest, making it directly useful for scaling PSG-based biomarker research in prodromal Parkinson's disease.
items.plain: Researchers took an AI system that automatically stages sleep from overnight brain recordings, trained it further on data from people with Parkinson's disease and a related sleep disorder, and tested it on a separate group of patients it had never seen. The AI's agreement with human experts improved after this extra training, and a confidence filter made its detection of REM sleep much more accurate, showing this tool could reliably speed up sleep studies in a hard-to-analyze patient group.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Multimodal Ultrasound Model for Prediction of Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Development and Validation.
items.body: OBJECTIVES: The primary aim of this study was to develop a multimodal artificial intelligence model for predicting spontaneous preterm birth using cervical 2-dimensional ultrasound and elastography images, as well as ultrasound parameters. METHODS: This prospective cohort study recruited pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound screening at 20-24 weeks of gestation. Participants were divided into spontaneous preterm birth group and full-term group. Three deep learning models were trained on images to compute scores via the best-performing model. Five supervised machine learning classifiers were developed and validated to predict spontaneous preterm birth based on ultrasound parameters and deep learning scores, and feature importance analysis was employed to visualize the importance of each feature in the model. RESULTS: A total of 721 pregnant women (44 with spontaneous preterm birth) were included. In deep learning models based on ultrasound images, DenseNet121 (AUC: 0.92/0.93) model exhibited excellent performance, and corresponding scores were obtained. Elasticity contrast index, hardness ratio, external os stiffness, Ratio, 2-dimension-score, and elastography-score were included to construct the 5 machine learning models. Among the multimodal models, the neural network model showed the best predictive performance in the validation set (AUC = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.73-0.96). Feature importance analysis revealed that both elastography-score and 2-dimension-score made significant contributions in a majority of the models. CONCLUSIONS: The multimodal artificial intelligence models using ultrasound parameters and cervical 2-dimensional ultrasound and elastography images demonstrated promising predictive capabilities in internal validation for spontaneous preterm birth in the second trimester. This offers assistance for intervention in patients at high risk of spontaneous preterm birth.
items.why: In a prospective cohort of 721 pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound at 20-24 weeks, a multimodal deep learning model combining cervical elastography and 2D ultrasound (DenseNet121, area under the curve or AUC 0.92-0.93) fed into machine learning classifiers achieved an AUC of 0.85 for predicting spontaneous preterm birth in an internal validation set. The prospective design and combination of imaging modalities are strengths, but validation was internal only and the outcome was rare (44 of 721 cases), so external replication is needed before clinical use.
items.plain: Doctors used ultrasound images and a measure of cervical stiffness, combined with AI, to try to predict which pregnant women would deliver early, testing this in a group of 721 women followed forward in time. The AI-based model correctly separated high and low risk women fairly well, but it was only tested on a held-out portion of the same original group, so it still needs to be checked in different hospitals and different women before doctors could rely on it.

items.title: Accelerated Biological Age as an Early Pregnancy Risk Factor for Preeclampsia.
items.body: BACKGROUND: The inability to predict risk in early pregnancy for preeclampsia represents a major limitation in prenatal care. OBJECTIVES: We used machine-learning approaches to identify early pregnancy features that distinguish women who develop preeclampsia from those with normotensive pregnancies, specifically focusing on the influence of maternal biological age. METHODS: Data were analyzed from a prospective cohort of pregnant women living in the upper Midwest (Midwest cohort) and from a cohort using publicly available data from the Prenatal Exposures & Preeclampsia Prevention Project (PEPP3). In both data sets, DNA methylation (DNAm) was quantified from blood samples collected in early pregnancy. Biological aging was estimated using established epigenetic clocks including Hannum, Horvath, and PhenoAge. Maternal data across pregnancy were collected via medical record abstraction. Predictors of preeclampsia were identified using LASSO regression and Random Forest. The potential predictive capacity of the selected features was evaluated by building logistic regression models with leave-one-out cross-validation and reporting performance metrics. RESULTS: In the Midwest cohort, accelerated biological aging per Hannum's epigenetic clock as well as higher chronological age and higher gestational weight gain were identified as important predictors of preeclampsia. Interestingly, only Hannum's epigenetic clock showed predictive power for preeclampsia. In the PEPP3 cohort, accelerated biological aging, as measured by Hannum's epigenetic clock, and chronological age were also identified as significant predictors of preeclampsia. DISCUSSION: Among women who developed preeclampsia, accelerated biological aging during early pregnancy may represent a risk biomarker that can be leveraged in clinical care. These findings identify a promising clinical indicator for preeclampsia risk, addressing a critical gap in screening and early diagnosis.
items.why: In two prospective cohorts, machine learning methods (LASSO regression and random forest) with leave-one-out cross-validation identified accelerated biological aging via the Hannum epigenetic clock, measured from early-pregnancy DNA methylation (DNAm), as a predictor distinguishing women who later developed preeclampsia from those with normotensive pregnancies. Replication of the Hannum clock finding across two independent cohorts strengthens the signal, though the study remains a biomarker discovery effort without external validation in a distinct population or a clinically deployable test.
items.plain: Scientists studied blood samples from early pregnancy in two separate groups of women and found that a measure of biological aging, calculated from chemical marks on DNA, could help predict who would later develop the dangerous pregnancy complication preeclampsia. Because the same finding showed up in two different groups, it is a more credible early-warning signal, but it still needs a larger, independent study before doctors could use it in the clinic.

items.title: Role prompting modulates linguistic style but not clinical decision structure in GPT-5 tumour board simulation.
items.body: Multidisciplinary tumour boards (MDTs) are the standard for gastrointestinal oncological decision-making but remain resource-intensive. Whether specialty-specific role prompting induces genuinely distinct clinical reasoning in large language models (LLMs)-or merely role-appropriate language around an invariant output-has not been systematically tested. We applied five zero-shot prompting frameworks and a majority-vote ensemble to GPT-5 across 100 gastrointestinal oncology cases with MDT-validated decisions: a simulated MDT, multi-expert deliberation, three specialist personas, and a majority-vote ensemble. Concordance with MDT recommendations ranged from 78% to 87%, with no significant inter-framework differences (Cochran's Q = 8.46, p = 0.133). Specialty-characteristic language was near-universal (97-100%) but uncorrelated with accuracy. Embedding analysis revealed high semantic similarity across personas (cosine similarity 0.805-0.836; η² = 0.049), contrasting with substantially greater output separation under multi-expert deliberation (η² = 0.554-0.581). GPT-5 reliably adapts linguistic style to clinical personas but produces limited specialty-specific output diversity, supporting its role as a decision-support adjunct rather than an autonomous specialist simulator.
items.why: In a zero-shot comparison across 100 gastrointestinal oncology cases, GPT-5 (a large language model, or LLM) prompted with different specialist personas matched multidisciplinary tumor board (MDT) recommendations 78-87% of the time with no significant difference between prompting frameworks, and embedding analysis showed personas produced near-identical semantic outputs despite highly distinct language. This suggests role prompting changes an LLM's tone but not its underlying clinical reasoning, an important caution for anyone considering these models as stand-ins for multi-specialist input rather than as a single decision-support adjunct.
items.plain: Scientists tested whether telling an AI chatbot to act like different medical specialists actually changes its medical advice, or just changes how it talks. Across 100 real cancer cases, the AI agreed with an actual team of doctors about 80 percent of the time no matter which specialist personality it was told to adopt, and its underlying recommendations were nearly identical between personas even though the wording sounded different, meaning the AI acts more like one advisor with different speaking styles than like several distinct experts.

items.title: Placental Blood-Flow Velocity Quantification From Diffusion MRI.
items.body: PURPOSE: Altered placental capillary blood flow is closely linked to obstetric complications, yet quantifying capillary-scale blood velocity remains challenging with existing imaging methods. This is partially because capillary networks form disordered microvascular beds at the voxel scale, rather than coherent, directional vessels. Here, we combine Monte Carlo (MC) simulations with machine learning to estimate placental capillary blood velocity directly from diffusion MRI (dMRI) data. METHODS: MC simulations incorporating perfusion and diffusion were performed to generate signal dictionaries for supervised machine learning regressors (random forest [RF] and multilayer perceptron [MLP]) to estimate velocity, perfusion fraction and diffusivity. The trained regressors were applied to simulated and in vivo dMRI data, with intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM)-based estimates as baselines for comparison. RESULTS: Our approach outperformed IVIM-based methods on simulated test data in recovering ground-truth parameters. Among the evaluated models, the MC-based MLP approach produced physiologically reasonable estimates of velocity in in vivo placentas, in agreement with previously reported measures and exhibited greater sensitivity than IVIM-generated methods. CONCLUSION: This study presents an approach to characterize capillary perfusion that alternates conventional IVIM models, particularly in organs such as the placenta, where pseudo-diffusion coefficient can be similar to tissue diffusion coefficient, limiting reliable IVIM parameter separation. Our method could enable detection of capillary blood-flow alterations, which could help identify pathological placental blood-flow conditions and potentially diagnosis relevant diseases, such as preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction. More broadly, the approach may translate to other organs where microscale blood-flow changes are key indicators of underlying pathologies.
items.why: This methods paper combines Monte Carlo simulations of placental capillary blood flow with machine learning regressors (random forest and multilayer perceptron) to estimate capillary blood velocity from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), outperforming conventional intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) fitting on simulated data and producing physiologically plausible in vivo estimates. This is an early-stage technical advance with potential relevance to preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction, but it lacks clinical outcome validation or a patient cohort linking the measure to disease.
items.plain: Scientists built an AI-assisted method to estimate how fast blood moves through the tiny blood vessels of the placenta using MRI scans, and showed it works better than older methods on simulated data and produces reasonable results in real placentas. This is a promising new measurement tool for detecting placenta problems like preeclampsia, but it has not yet been tested to see if it actually predicts these conditions in patients.

items.title: Automated early preterm detection using hybrid multimodal attention network with gated fusion.
items.body: Preterm birth is a major pregnancy complication associated with increased maternal and neonatal risks, making early detection of labor essential. Electrohysterography (EHG), provides a non-invasive approach for monitoring uterine dynamics. However, global synchronization patterns and propagation dynamics remain insufficiently understood, and many existing methods rely on manual annotation, limiting clinical applicability. This study evaluates synchronization-driven propagation patterns in multi-electrode EHG signals and proposes an automated framework for early preterm detection, beyond the commonly studied one-week prediction window before delivery. The analysis included 452 recordings from pregnancies between 21 and 36 weeks of gestation, covering spontaneous, cesarean, induced, and induced-cesarean cases. Four electrode configurations (S1-S2, S1-S3, S2-S3, and Multichannel) were examined. A hybrid deep learning model integrating multi-head attention and a gated fusion mechanism was used to combine EHG segments with synchronization features. Feature selection was performed using random forest top-k selection, and class imbalance was handled through inverse-frequency weighting. Results showed that non-linear synchronization measures, including non-linear interdependence directionality index and normalized permutation cross mutual information, were statistically significant (p<0.05) and provided strong discrimination. Our results suggest increased synchronization and spatial coordination near term, with relatively stronger activity in the upper right uterine region. In contrast, preterm activity appeared weaker and less organized. The model achieved an accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.98, 0.93, 0.99, 0.94, and 0.99, respectively, indicating robust performance. These findings highlight synchronization as a key marker for early and clinically relevant preterm detection.
items.why: This retrospective single-dataset study trained a hybrid deep learning model with multi-head attention and gated fusion on 452 electrohysterography (EHG) recordings to detect preterm labor earlier than the standard one-week prediction window, reporting an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.99 and sensitivity of 0.93 using synchronization features between uterine electrodes. The near-perfect performance metrics and lack of external validation on an independent cohort raise strong concerns about overfitting, so despite the appealing reproductive relevance this needs replication before it changes clinical practice.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI model that reads electrical signals from the uterus (picked up by skin sensors) to try to predict premature labor earlier than current methods, testing it on data from 452 pregnancies. The model scored almost perfectly, but because it was only tested on the same type of data it was trained on and not checked against a separate, independent group of patients, this near-perfect result is likely too good to be true and needs to be confirmed elsewhere.

scored.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
scored.why: A deep neural network (U-Sleep) pretrained on 19,236 polysomnograms (PSGs) was finetuned on multicenter Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) cohorts and evaluated on an independent clinical hold-out, improving staging agreement (Cohen's kappa) from 0.60 to 0.64, with a confidence threshold raising REM sleep detection precision from 85% to 95.6%. This is a rare example of a publicly available, externally validated automated sleep staging tool tested specifically in neurodegenerative disease populations where manual scoring is hardest, making it directly useful for scaling PSG-based biomarker research in prodromal Parkinson's disease.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Multimodal Ultrasound Model for Prediction of Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Development and Validation.
scored.why: In a prospective cohort of 721 pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound at 20-24 weeks, a multimodal deep learning model combining cervical elastography and 2D ultrasound (DenseNet121, area under the curve or AUC 0.92-0.93) fed into machine learning classifiers achieved an AUC of 0.85 for predicting spontaneous preterm birth in an internal validation set. The prospective design and combination of imaging modalities are strengths, but validation was internal only and the outcome was rare (44 of 721 cases), so external replication is needed before clinical use.

scored.title: Accelerated Biological Age as an Early Pregnancy Risk Factor for Preeclampsia.
scored.why: In two prospective cohorts, machine learning methods (LASSO regression and random forest) with leave-one-out cross-validation identified accelerated biological aging via the Hannum epigenetic clock, measured from early-pregnancy DNA methylation (DNAm), as a predictor distinguishing women who later developed preeclampsia from those with normotensive pregnancies. Replication of the Hannum clock finding across two independent cohorts strengthens the signal, though the study remains a biomarker discovery effort without external validation in a distinct population or a clinically deployable test.

scored.title: Role prompting modulates linguistic style but not clinical decision structure in GPT-5 tumour board simulation.
scored.why: In a zero-shot comparison across 100 gastrointestinal oncology cases, GPT-5 (a large language model, or LLM) prompted with different specialist personas matched multidisciplinary tumor board (MDT) recommendations 78-87% of the time with no significant difference between prompting frameworks, and embedding analysis showed personas produced near-identical semantic outputs despite highly distinct language. This suggests role prompting changes an LLM's tone but not its underlying clinical reasoning, an important caution for anyone considering these models as stand-ins for multi-specialist input rather than as a single decision-support adjunct.

scored.title: Placental Blood-Flow Velocity Quantification From Diffusion MRI.
scored.why: This methods paper combines Monte Carlo simulations of placental capillary blood flow with machine learning regressors (random forest and multilayer perceptron) to estimate capillary blood velocity from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), outperforming conventional intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) fitting on simulated data and producing physiologically plausible in vivo estimates. This is an early-stage technical advance with potential relevance to preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction, but it lacks clinical outcome validation or a patient cohort linking the measure to disease.

scored.title: Automated early preterm detection using hybrid multimodal attention network with gated fusion.
scored.why: This retrospective single-dataset study trained a hybrid deep learning model with multi-head attention and gated fusion on 452 electrohysterography (EHG) recordings to detect preterm labor earlier than the standard one-week prediction window, reporting an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.99 and sensitivity of 0.93 using synchronization features between uterine electrodes. The near-perfect performance metrics and lack of external validation on an independent cohort raise strong concerns about overfitting, so despite the appealing reproductive relevance this needs replication before it changes clinical practice.

scored.title: Navigating fairness in artificial intelligence-based prediction models: theoretical constructs and practical applications.
scored.why: This Viewpoint reviews 27 definitions of fairness for artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical prediction models and argues that clinical utility, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, and statistical parity are the most useful group-based metrics, illustrated through two use cases. It is a conceptual synthesis rather than new empirical work, useful for framing fairness audits but offering no new data or validated tool.

scored.title: Integrative computational toxicology and experimental validation unveils ESR1-mediated steroidogenic disruption in triphenyl phosphate-induced female reproductive toxicity.
scored.why: Using network toxicology, transcriptomics, and machine learning on public datasets, this study prioritized ESR1 (estrogen receptor alpha) as the key gene mediating triphenyl phosphate-induced disruption of steroidogenesis, with an exploratory external evaluation area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94 and confirmatory in vitro knockdown experiments. The machine learning step is a hypothesis-generating prioritization tool within a mechanistic toxicology pipeline, not a clinical prediction model, limiting direct relevance to patient care.

scored.title: Causal associations between hormone replacement therapy and brain structure: Evidence from large-scale Mendelian randomization and double machine learning.
scored.why: Using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and double machine learning (DML) on UK Biobank genome-wide association study (GWAS) data, this study found causal associations between hormone replacement therapy (HRT) timing and use and specific brain structural features across 1,366 imaging phenotypes, with independent DML validation supporting the MR findings for several associations. The large sample and dual-method triangulation strengthen causal claims, but the outcomes are structural brain measures rather than clinical endpoints, and one key finding was excluded due to pleiotropy.

scored.title: From pixels to patterns: the AI revolution in stem cell-derived models.
scored.why: This Perspective surveys how deep learning, convolutional neural networks, and foundation models are being applied to image-based analysis of stem cell-derived embryo models and organoids, covering phenotyping, drug screening, and fate prediction. It is a narrative overview with no new experiments or validation data, so its value is orientation rather than evidence.

scored.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy reduces regulatory T-cells in cervical cancer.
scored.why: In 64 patients from a randomized cervical cancer trial, multiplex immunohistochemistry with a validated machine-learning image analysis platform (ImmuNet) quantified immune cell populations before and after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT), finding reduced regulatory T-cell (Treg) density post-treatment associated with better overall survival. The machine learning tool here serves only as an image quantification aid within an oncology immunology study, with no algorithmic innovation or clinical AI evaluation to speak of.

scored.title: Exploring Perceptions of Leveraging AI to Improve Outcomes in Maternal, Sexual, and Reproductive Health in Sub-Saharan Africa: Exploratory Qualitative Study.
scored.why: This qualitative study interviewed 59 stakeholders in sub-Saharan Africa about perceptions of AI for maternal, sexual, and reproductive health, using framework analysis to surface themes like trust and equity concerns. It contains no AI system, deployment, or outcome data, offering context on attitudes rather than evidence of clinical impact.

scored.title: Data-driven insights in menopause: A scoping review of sensors and AI.
scored.why: This scoping review of 58 studies maps sensor-based and data-driven approaches to menopause symptom monitoring, finding weak and inconsistent associations for measures like heart rate variability and highlighting a lack of standardized ground truth across studies. As a review with no new data, it mainly documents immaturity in the field rather than providing an actionable finding.

scored.title: Bridging the Diagnostic Gap: Reviewing Current Endometriosis Screening Tools and Models.
scored.why: This scoping review of 18 studies on endometriosis screening tools categorizes questionnaire-based, app-based, machine learning, and subtype-focused models, reporting area under the curve (AUC) values from 0.77 to 0.95 with machine learning models performing best, but notes significant gaps in external validation and cultural adaptation across all tools. As a review it identifies the field's state but adds no new evidence or validated instrument.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Multi-Omics Biomarker Discovery in Ectopic Pregnancy: A Comprehensive Review.
scored.why: This narrative review synthesizes 52 studies from 1988-2026 on machine learning, multi-omics, and robotic surgery in ectopic pregnancy, citing area under the curve (AUC) values up to 0.929 for methotrexate failure prediction, but explicitly notes that retrospective designs and small samples limit generalizability. As a review with no new data or prospective validation, it mainly catalogs existing fragmented evidence rather than advancing the field.

scored.title: [Clinical and preprocedural factors influencing in vitro fertilization outcomes: a machine learning-based analysis].
scored.why: This narrative review of the University of Szeged's Gametogenesis Research Group and other literature summarizes machine learning-identified predictors of in vitro fertilization (IVF) success, consistently highlighting maternal age and embryo quality as the strongest factors. It presents no new model, dataset, or validation, functioning as a synthesis of already-known predictors rather than a novel contribution.

scored.title: Identification of genomic features that uniquely impact estrogen receptor alpha binding and its effects on gene expression in endometrial cancer.
scored.why: This basic science study applies machine learning to genomic data from estrogen receptor alpha (ER)-positive endometrial and breast cancer cell lines to identify factors predicting ER binding at estrogen response elements (EREs), pinpointing SOX17 as an endometrial-specific regulator and confirming it with a CRISPR knockout screen. The work is mechanistic cell-line research using machine learning as an analytic tool, with no clinical prediction, patient cohort, or translational validation presented.

scored.title: Oura Seeks Patent To Detect Pregnancy Complications
scored.why: This item reports that a wearable technology company is seeking a patent for a pulse wave velocity sensing system intended to flag early signs of hypertension, preeclampsia, and gestational diabetes, but no clinical data, validation study, or device has been described. A patent filing signals future intent rather than a demonstrated capability, so this is speculative rather than evidence-based news.

scored.title: AbCellera’s Menopause Drug Cuts Hot Flashes by 83% in Phase 2 Trial
scored.why: This item reports positive Phase 2 randomized controlled trial (RCT) results for a nonhormonal antibody treatment for menopausal hot flashes, with an 83% reduction in frequency in a 92-patient trial, but the intervention is a monoclonal antibody drug with no artificial intelligence or algorithmic component. Despite being a rigorous clinical trial, it falls outside this digest's AI-focused scope and should be read as background industry news rather than a clinical AI advance.

scored.title: New Startup Launches to Close the Bedside Communication Gap in Hospitals
scored.why: This announcement describes a new startup launching an ambient artificial intelligence platform that records hospital bedside conversations and generates shared task lists, with a pilot planned at a major academic medical center but no outcome data yet available. It is an early-stage product launch worth noting for context but has no evaluation to assess its clinical impact.

scored.title: Abbott, Google to combine glucose data with AI coaching
scored.why: This is a partnership announcement pairing Abbott's over-the-counter continuous glucose monitor (Lingo) with Google's health app for AI-driven coaching, but no product details, algorithm description, or clinical evidence are given. It has no reproductive or clinical AI evaluation content and reads as a business development note rather than a study or deployment with outcomes.

scored.title: Enriching Clinical Trials With Machine Learning.
scored.why: This JAMA piece on enriching clinical trials with machine learning has no abstract or text provided, so no findings, methods, or evidence can be assessed. Without substantive content this cannot be judged as a meaningful contribution this week.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence must not worsen maternal health inequalities.
scored.why: This is a commentary titled 'Artificial intelligence must not worsen maternal health inequalities' with no abstract or text provided, so its argument, evidence, or specific recommendations cannot be assessed. Without content this is scored conservatively as an opinion piece of uncertain substance.

scored.title: Antibiotic mixture exposure in meconium affects child neurodevelopment via altering early-life gut microbiome and metabolome.
scored.why: This cohort study of 300 mother-infant pairs used interpretable machine learning and mediation analysis to link meconium-measured antibiotic burden to lower Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ) neurodevelopmental scores at 6 months, with Lactobacillus and a metabolite proposed as mediators. The analysis is environmental epidemiology using machine learning as a statistical tool rather than a clinical AI application, and findings are explicitly hypothesis-generating and unreplicated.

scored.title: Precision Medicine in Transfusion-Dependent and Non-Transfusion-Dependent β-Thalassemia: Toward Personalized Diagnosis and Therapy.
scored.why: This narrative review covers precision medicine strategies in transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia, mentioning artificial intelligence (AI) only briefly as having 'its strongest role in screening and diagnosis' without describing any specific AI method or evidence. The topic sits outside reproductive medicine and clinical AI evaluation entirely, making it low priority for this digest.

scored.title: Emerging frontiers in cervical cancer diagnostics: Recent innovations in biosensors for HPV detection.
scored.why: This is a narrative review of biosensor technologies for human papillomavirus (HPV) detection in cervical cancer screening, with only a passing mention of artificial intelligence and machine learning rather than any new data or evaluation. It contains no original study, trial, or validated model, so it offers little actionable information for a reader tracking clinical AI advances.
